newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador says new oil deal with Maxus now ready.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says new oil deal with Maxus now ready.

text.p: Ecuador's Energy and Mines minister Alfredo Adum said on Thursday a new deal between state firm Petroecuador and U.S. Maxus Energy, a unit of Argentinian oil giant YPF SA, was ready for signing.

Last month the new government of President Abdala Bucaram banned Maxus, which has been producing oil in the country for nine years, from operating in Ecuador, saying the Dallas-based firm was not honouring its contract obligation to share profits with Petroecuador.
But Adum told Congress on Thursday that the new contract should allow Maxus to resume operations.
"Maxus will have to hand over to the Ecuadoran state 29 barrels of oil for every 100 barrels it produces," he said.

The new contract foresees a joint venture rather than a third-party system as in the past, Adum said. He said other foreign firms operating in Ecuador such as ARCO, Oryx Energy , Occidental Petroleum Corp and Elf Aquitaine would also have to go into joint ventures with Petroecuador.
Ecuador, which in 1992 quit the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries, last year produced an average 380,000 barrels per day.
